summary: AstroHealth is a health monitoring app that helps astronauts check their own health on long missions, understand what changes mean, and know when to contact flight surgeons.
details:
AstroHealth is an app that assist astronauts with monitoring their health during long missions. The astronaut inputs their health metrics, such as heart rate, blood pressure, sleep hours, and stress level and it gets saved to the device. After submitting health metrics, the astronaut has access to a body map, AI analysis and assistant, and a look at their physical/mental health stats. The body map displays each body region and ties its status to a spaceflight hazard, such as fluid shift, radiation, or isolation. The app is easy to understand for astronauts, providing explanations and next steps are written for non-experts, with color-coded statuses. The project was created with React, Node.js, SQLite, Google Gemini API, assistance from AI agents, and NASA data.

In the future, we'd like to connect all screens to live data from the backend, add trend charts, and provide access to a library of medically reviewed procedures. We also plan to integrate wearable health-monitoring devices, so astronauts can automatically track and update their health measurements without manually entering data. The system could detect unusual health patterns and send alerts when potential health risks are identified. Additionally, we want to introduce offline functionality, allowing astronauts to access their health records and medical guidance even without an internet connection. When communication with Earth is available, astronauts would also be able to contact medical professionals on Earth for further assistance, share their health reports, and receive guidance despite communication delays during long-distance space missions.
